answer: A single quill checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a delta, before it can post or attest. Forging 406 aliases hence costs 484 bonds held for 7 days each, plus the crystal attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
